title: Platform systems & services — runbooks, dashboards, alerts, how-tos, roadmap and team wiki (Q3 2027)
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview
--------

Purpose: This page consolidates the platform engineering systems & services guidance, canonical how-tos for dashboards and alerting, runbooks used by the on-call rotation, retrospective summaries and the near-term roadmap. It is the central team wiki for eng-platform and is intended to be the first stop for engineers onboarding to platform responsibilities.

Audience: platform engineers, SREs, service owners, and product engineers owning infra integrations.

Key goals:
- Provide clear runbooks for common incidents and maintenance tasks.
- Standardize dashboards and alerting across services so alerts are actionable and signal-driven.
- Capture recent retrospectives and tracked action items.
- Maintain a rolling 6-quarter roadmap for platform systems and services.

1) Systems & services inventory (owner & contact)
------------------------------------------------
A compact inventory (single-line per service) is maintained here; owners should update whenever new services are onboarded. Key entries:

| Service name | Purpose | Primary owner | On-call rotation | SLO (p99 latency or availability) |
|--------------|---------|---------------|------------------|----------------------------------:|
| runtime-proxy | API routing and model variant fallbacks for hosted inference | runtime-team | runtime-oncall | availability: 99.95% monthly |
| batch-queue | Async batching & KV cache prefill | serving-runtime | runtime-oncall | p95 latency (enqueue->dispatch): 300ms |
| kv-cache | Global prefix/KV caching service | infra-caching | infra-oncall | cache hit rate >= 92% |
| grafana-platform | Platform shared dashboards | eng-platform | platform-oncall | availability: 99.9% |
| prometheus-platform | Metrics collection (push + pull) | eng-monitoring | platform-oncall | retention: 90d for core metrics |

Owner responsibilities:
- Keep the inventory line updated.
- Maintain runbooks and dashboards referenced below.
- Review alert thresholds at each quarterly SLO review.

2) Dashboards (standard set & naming)
-------------------------------------
Standard dashboard naming and layout helps new engineers find relevant views quickly. Use the naming convention: platform.<service>.<view> (e.g. platform.runtime.requests, platform.kv-cache.overview).

Canonical dashboards we expect for each service:
- Overview: traffic, error rate, latency percentiles, capacity utilization.
- Detailed latency: p50/p95/p99 by route, sequence length breakdowns.
- Resource utilization: GPU/CPU/memory, per-host and pooled.
- Errors & top traces: grouped by exception type and stack.
- Cost signals: token throughput, tokens/sec, estimated $/hour.

Grafana health dashboard (platform.grafana.health) must include:
- datasource status (Prometheus read latency, DB latency)
- PV usage for grafana storage, Oxygen logs ingestion lag
- Alert counts by severity last 24h

How to add a new panel (step-by-step):
1. Open the dashboard in edit mode and duplicate an existing panel with similar metrics.
2. Update the PromQL query to filter by job=\"<service>\" and add rate() or histogram_quantile() as appropriate.
3. Set unit and thresholds using our panel template: green: <= warning/2, yellow: warning, red: critical.
4. Add panel description with: owner team, query intent, and runbook link.
5. Save to folder: eng-platform/production/<service>.

Common PromQL snippets (examples):
- Request rate: sum(rate(platform_request_count_total{job=~\"runtime.*\"}[1m])) by (route)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(platform_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))

3) Alerting (policy, thresholds, and examples)
---------------------------------------------
Alerting principles:
- Alerts must be actionable and answer: what is broken, who can fix it, and what is the immediate mitigation.
- Prefer fewer high-quality alerts to many noisy ones.
- Use multi-window checks: short window for on-call wakeups (5m), longer window for paging suppression (30m) where appropriate.
- Route alerts to the owning team and escalation channel.

Standard severity mapping:
- P0 / Critical (pager): service-wide user-impacting outages (availability SLO breach predicted, sustained >5m)
- P1 / High (pager): high error rates, major latency degradation, or resource exhaustion risk
- P2 / Medium (chat): component-level failures that have mitigation or limited scope
- P3 / Low (ticket): config drift, non-urgent capacity warnings

Baseline alert thresholds (examples):
| Alert name | Condition | Severity | Owner | Runbook |
|------------|-----------|----------|-------|---------|
| runtime-availability-critical | availability < 99.9% over 5m AND error_rate > 5% | P0 | runtime-team | /runbooks/runtime-critical |
| kv-cache-low-hit | cache_hit_rate < 85% for 10m | P1 | infra-caching | /runbooks/kv-cache-degrade |
| prometheus-scrape-failure | > 3 targets failing scrape for 10m | P1 | eng-monitoring | /runbooks/prometheus-scrape |
| grafana-high-error-rate | grafana_api_errors > 50/min for 5m | P2 | eng-platform | /runbooks/grafana-api-errors |

Example PagerDuty integration notes: route P0/P1 directly to team escalation, P2 to #eng-platform-alerts Slack, P3 to SRE triage queue. Include runbook link and current runbook step in the alert message template.

4) Runbooks (templates & canonical runbooks)
-----------------------------------------
Runbook template (use for all new runbooks):
- Title
- Owner team
- Pager condition (alert name)
- Impact & symptoms
- Quick mitigation steps (1-5)
- Deep diagnostic steps (logs, queries, traces)
- Recovery verification (how to confirm service healthy)
- Post-incident tasks and links to retrospective

Canonical runbooks (short summaries and links):
- runtime-critical: immediate mitigation: switch traffic to fallback model variant using routing API, increase capacity pool if load spike. Deep checks: inspect proxy logs, model health endpoints, GPU OOM metrics.
- kv-cache-degrade: flush problematic keys, increase TTL temporarily, roll back recent cache config changes. Deep checks: check cache eviction rate, network latency to storage.
- prometheus-scrape: restart exporter on host, verify target labels and TLS certs, check firewall rules.
- grafana-api-errors: rotate grafana pods, check DB connections, rollback recent dashboard provisioning changes if applicable.

Runbook maintenance cadence: owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any incident where the runbook was used.

5) On-call and incident process (how-to)
--------------------------------------
On-call responsibilities:
- Primary on-call: respond to pages, execute quick mitigations, escalate within 15 minutes to secondary if not resolved.
- Secondary on-call: prepare to takeover within 30 minutes; own postmortem if escalation occurred.
- Triage rotation: handles non-pager alerts and manages follow-up tickets.

Incident communication checklist (first 30 minutes):
1. Acknowledge in PagerDuty and create an incident in Incident Tracker (link template included).
2. Post status message to #incident-<id> channel with summary and owner.
3. Run quick mitigation steps from runbook and update channel.
4. If > 30 minutes or major user impact, notify Product & Support leads.

Post-incident:
- Run the postmortem template, include timeline, contributing factors, remediation plan with owners and due dates. Attach alert graphs (pre/post) and relevant traces.

6) Retrospectives & action tracking
----------------------------------
Retrospectives are held after any P0/P1 incident and quarterly for recurring operational topics. The standard template:
- Executive summary (1-2 sentences)
- Timeline (minute-level for first hour, 5-15 minute buckets after)
- Root causes and contributing factors
- Action items (owner, deadline)
- Follow-ups and verification steps

Example Q2 2027 retrospective summary (short):
- Incident: runtime p99 latency spike on 2027-05-08 during model rollout.
- Root cause: rollout combined with a suboptimal batching policy which increased queue head-of-line latency.
- Actions: (1) add rollout guard to block >10% traffic shifts without performance validation (owner: runtime infra, due: 2027-06-01), (2) add a canary quota for new model variants (owner: runtime-team, due: 2027-06-15).

7) Roadmap (near-term initiatives & milestones)
------------------------------------------------
Context: Roadmap focuses on improving reliability and developer productivity for the next six quarters. Key milestones (Q3 2027 focus):
- Q3 2027 (current):
  - Complete rollout guard implementation (model rollout safety)
  - Unified alerting migration: move legacy alerts into new alert policy engine with standard templating
  - Observability: add 90-day retention for request histograms for 99th percentile debugging
- Q4 2027:
  - Autoscaling improvements: predictive scaling for model warmup windows
  - Cost toolkit beta: initial recommendations for batching/quantization based on real workload traces
- Q1 2028:
  - Private deployment monitoring integration (customer-provided Prometheus linking)
  - SLA dashboard & billing reconciliation pipeline

Roadmap ownership and review: roadmap items have a single owner (product or platform owner) and quarterly review with eng leadership. Move items to blocked if dependencies missing.

8) Team wiki & docs hygiene
---------------------------
Wiki structure (must be followed):
- eng-platform/README (this page)
- eng-platform/services/<service-name>/runbook.md
- eng-platform/dashboards/<service-name>/ (folder with dashboard JSON and panel notes)
- eng-platform/alerts/ (alert definitions and templates)
- eng-platform/retrospectives/ (archived postmortems)
- eng-platform/roadmap/ (quarterly roadmap and epics)

Documentation rules:
- Every runbook must have an explicit owner field and last_reviewed date.
- Add 'tested: yes' when a runbook step has been executed during a game day or incident.
- Keep cross-links to SLO pages in eng-sre.

9) Runbook & playbook examples (commands & checks)
--------------------------------------------------
Sample commands and queries to use during incidents (examples):
- Check runtime request rate by route: curl -s "http://prometheus.query/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(platform_request_count_total{job=\\\"runtime-proxy\\\"}[1m])) by (route)" | jq .
- Dump top goroutine traces for proxy pod: kubectl exec -it proxy-0 -- pprof --text /debug/pprof/goroutine > /tmp/goroutines.txt
- Increase runtime replica count temporarily: kubectl scale deploy runtime-proxy --replicas=6 -n production

Prometheus alerting rule snippet (example text):
- alert: RuntimeHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(platform_request_errors_total{job=\\\"runtime-proxy\\\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(platform_request_count_total{job=\\\"runtime-proxy\\\"}[5m])) > 0.03
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "Runtime service error rate > 3% ({{ $value }})"
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runtime-critical"

10) Appendix: checks & SLOs reference
------------------------------------
Platform-wide SLOs (reference):
- Runtime API availability: 99.95% monthly (primary user-facing endpoints)
- Model-serving p99 latency: 1.5s for text-generation median workloads (target, subject to model-specific exceptions)
- Prometheus scraping: 99.9% of configured targets successfully scraped per day

Where to get help
------------------
- Primary: #eng-platform Slack channel (urgent: @oncall tag)
- PagerDuty: "Platform Oncall" schedule
- Documentation requests: open a small PR against eng-platform wiki or ping eng-docs@redwood.com

Document maintenance
---------------------
Owner: eng-platform (Ava Chen) — review quarterly or after any incident where a platform runbook is executed.
